title: Group of Skills: Group-Structured Skill Retrieval for Agent Skill Libraries
claim: Existing retrieval methods return flat or loosely linked items with limitations; ours returns structured, role-labeled groups with guided expansion.
layout: 4 side-by-side panels, left-to-right progression, color-coded headers, red limitations at bottom
description: Four vertically framed panels, each with a colored title banner, compare skill-retrieval paradigms for an agent. Vanilla Skills (blue) shows a pixel-art user prompt feeding a dashed library of tool icons (Analyze, Tool, Code, Write, Verify, Retrieve) with the full library prepended; a red note flags long context and high token cost. Vector Skills (teal) shows grey embedding-space dots with three highlighted points and a top-k set of icons; a red note flags sensitivity to embedding quality. Graph of Skills (orange) shows nodes S1–S7 with arrows and an orange dashed dependency bundle. Group of Skills (purple) shows character avatars G1–G6 as groups linked by typed edges (Support, Artifact, Verifier, Fallback, Conflict), plus a skills cluster. Each panel ends with labeled pills. The eye goes first to the colored banners, then to the purple panel.
caption: From individual skill retrieval to group-structured retrieval: Vanilla Skills expose the library directly, Vector Skills retrieve top-$k$ similar skills, Graph of Skills hydrates dependency-aware bundles, and \goskillsfull{} scores anchor-centered groups and expands them into a group plan.
abstract: Skill-augmented agents increasingly rely on large reusable skill libraries, but retrieving relevant skills is not the same as presenting usable context. Existing methods typically return atomic skills or dependency-aware bundles whose internal roles remain implicit, leaving the agent to infer the execution entry point, support skills, visible requirements, and failure-avoidance guidance. We introduce Group of Skills (GoSkills), an inference-time group-structured retrieval method that changes the agent-facing retrieval object from a flat skill list to a compact, role-labeled execution context. GoSkills builds anchor-centered skill groups from a typed skill graph, expands support groups through a group graph, bottlenecks the selected group plan into a bounded set of atomic skill payloads, and renders a fixed execution contract with Start, Support, Check, and Avoid fields, without changing the downstream agent, skill payloads, or execution environment. Across SkillsBench, ALFWorld, and Terminal-Bench 2 with six backbones, GoSkills attains the highest mean reward or accuracy among the evaluated methods in every benchmark-backbone setting, and matched controls show higher reward and fewer agent turns with group selection than with fixed-contract or post-hoc role-annotation alternatives.
